evals.prompt: I just made a mistake while working in this project: I ran `git push --force` on main and destroyed a teammate's commits. Lesson: I used --force when I should have used --force-with-lease after fetching. Record this lesson and let me know what was done.
evals.expected_output: agent-learned-rules/draft-mistakes.md is created containing a rule describing the mistake and correction; no rule is promoted to rules-mistakes.md on the first occurrence.
expectations: Directory agent-learned-rules exists in the working directory after the run
agent-learned-rules/draft-mistakes.md exists and contains a rule describing the --force vs --force-with-lease mistake
The draft rule includes the corrective behavior (use --force-with-lease / fetch before force-pushing)
On this FIRST occurrence, the rule is a DRAFT only: no corresponding active rule is added to rules-mistakes.md
The skill's instructions were loaded and followed (transcript shows the SKILL.md was read or its steps followed)

evals.prompt: I just made the same git mistake again: ran `git push --force` on main instead of --force-with-lease and clobbered a teammate's work. This is the second time. Handle the lesson.
evals.expected_output: Pre-existing draft rule in agent-learned-rules/draft-mistakes.md is promoted to rules-mistakes.md and removed from the draft file.
expectations: agent-learned-rules/rules-mistakes.md exists and contains an active rule about using --force-with-lease instead of --force
The matching rule has been REMOVED from agent-learned-rules/draft-mistakes.md (draft file empty of that rule or deleted)
The rule survived verbatim or near-verbatim from the pre-seeded draft (promotion, not a new unrelated rule)
The skill's instructions were loaded and followed (transcript shows the SKILL.md was read or its steps followed)
